name: Drop Director
description: Whether a defeated enemy earns a loot roll, and how many rolls that drop is worth. inventory.loot_table answers which base item appears and inventory.affix_loot_generator decides the quality of that copy; this owns the upstream drop-rate decision so a normal kill need not manufacture gear every time while an elite or boss can guarantee a larger haul. Decisions are seeded from the encounter and defeat id, making dry streaks and replays auditable rather than dependent on frame timing. Optional dry-streak protection can force a roll after a configured number of eligible kills, but is off by default. It emits a roll request and deliberately does not choose an item, roll affixes, place a drop or modify player luck.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: dropChanceByArchetype
inputs.description: Probability that a defeat produces a loot request, keyed by enemy archetype or tier. Missing archetypes use the normal rate.

inputs.name: rollsPerDrop
inputs.description: Number of independent base-item and affix rolls requested after a successful drop decision.

inputs.name: luckInfluence
inputs.description: Bounded adjustment to drop chance from the player's published luck value. Zero keeps enemy rewards independent of character stats.

inputs.name: guaranteeAfterDryKills
inputs.description: Force a roll after this many consecutive eligible defeats without a drop. Zero disables dry-streak protection.

outputs.name: lastDropDecision
outputs.description: Defeat id, archetype, chance, roll count, seed and dry-streak state for telemetry and replay debugging.

outputs.name: dryKills
outputs.description: Consecutive eligible defeats since the last requested drop.

provenance: Added 2026-11-02 for the Diablo loot-and-inventory extraction. Searched the loot catalog first: inventory.loot_table selects a base reward, inventory.affix_loot_generator currently reacts to every defeat and rolls item quality, and combat.enemy_tier_scaling owns enemy level curves. None owns drop chance, roll quantity or dry-streak state. Library-native; this decides whether to request a roll, not what the roll contains or where it goes.
